questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to participate in the world wide renowned Marine Program at Boston University since I am studying Marine Biology

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The Marine Program is a reseach based semester. It is a lot of work and I did not have any time to explore the US or Boston, since we were on research vessels and excursions almost all the time. It was great but also very demanding.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Sage gave us assistance and all important information

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Sage was extremely busy before we arrived at BU, so she could not help as much as might have been required. The website of BU was very helpful though.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was extremely difficult and although you might save a little bit of money living off campus, I wouldnt recommend it to anyone. First, I had to move to another airbnb, since I booked the first one in Dorchester (quite close to campus) and did not know that the area was dangerous. I moved to Newton which is a safe area but also an hour away from campus. Shortly, please just book on campus housing, it will save you a lot of time and nerves.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is also extremely expensive, not really cheaper than on campus. Plus, you might find an airbnb located in a dangerous area, such as Dorchester, Roxbury and Mattapan where daily shootings and stabbings happen. DON'T BOOK ANYTHING THERE!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I went to several different dormatories of exchange students and other american students: the apartment style dorm was the nicest, since you would usually only live with one other person and this way you could keep your apartment clean. However, the shared bathroom dorms where you would only have your own room and no kitchen, a shared bad with 6 others, were horrible- super disgusting, old and expensive (1200$ monthly) anyway.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The registration happened through
Ku.net
. All information was available there. Also, Pernille Winther was helpful and gave us all information.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help from KU website and Pernille Winther

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was told I could not take any courses from the Marine Program, so I registered for different courses. When I started my courses at BU, I spoke to all professors and they helped me get into the courses that I wanted. The professors are extremely kind and helpful and want to make the best out of your stay. It is only the system that is a problem usually, so don't worry if the system tells you that you are not allowed to take a specific course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If none of your preferred courses are available for registration, do not worry. Register for other courses and meet the professor at BU as soon as possible when you arrive. They will be happy to help you transfer to different courses. Once you get the apporval of a professor, the system usually lets you change your course as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The BUMP program was incredible, with highly skilled professors, best equipped laboratories and real research based coursework.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: every course which has the number 500 or above is considered a MA course

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was research based teaching. The BUMP program consisted of several research projects in student groups of 2-3 people. The professors were also eager to teach and explain, they really loved teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
• CAS BI521 Quant Fisheries, 4 credits=10 ECTS-point
• CAS EE544 Coastal Sediments, 4 credits=10 ECTS-point
• CAS EE591 Bio-optic Oceanography, 4 credits=10 ECTS-point

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All courses of the Marine Program due to the research based coursework. The Quantitative Fisheries class however was a coding class, so it was math heavy and difficult for most students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I changed the airbnb once I got to the US, since the neighbourhood was not the best. Usually, one room in an airbnb costs 85$ a night, if it is in a safe neighbourhood. Everything below cannot be safe.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food, rent, transportation, everything is more expensive. Boston is considered to be the most expensive city in the US, even more than New York.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything imagineable. I recommend attending the Splash event in the first two weeks of the semester, where all student organizations of BU are shown and give away free merch. The fitrec center offers various fitness classes. Some museums are also free for BU students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Fitrec classes, they offer everything free of charge for exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit New york, walk around Boston, there is so much to see but stay in the safe areas please. I recommend following Instagram accounts that showcase the "best Boston cafes, museums" etc., you could find some hidden gems

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The american culture is very easy going and outgoing. However, really close do you rarely get to american students. They might party a lot and might be loud etc. but it is not a very personal culture. I would recommend getting to know the other exchange students since you are all in the same boat.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is quite easy to get into conversations with americans, they are mostly loud and outgoing.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found it very challenging that american students are this loud and non discrete. I bounded mostly with other exchange students and even the Professors who were rather discrete and calm.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness, the students were mostly interested and kind, although I did not like that they seemed loud and "rough".

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy the experience at an american university, everything is different, from the very first day on: loud music, big colorful screens and screams to welcome the new students
2. Since everything is so different, try not to get too overwhelmed, but keep contact to your family and friends back home, it will help you "survive" in the loud messy american system
3. Enjoy the privilege that us exchange students do not have to pay the annnual 90k$ tuition fees and be aware of the fact that you will be surrounded by american students either coming from rich families or students that have the best grades and have already been to Harvard University, Cambridge University and whatever before. It is a different environment than at KU, definitely.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just to repeat myself: book housing on campus, no matter how disgusting the housing is (in case the other students dont help in the cleaning process), you safe lots of time and nerves living on campus and having a meal plan. The full meal plan is also much cheaper and saves time than having to buy groceries and cook every day. Almost every exchange student that I got to know had a meal plan and all students were living on campus.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing the incredible reasearch facilities at one of the best american universities (which has a lot of money)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To keep up with daily life activities (cooking food, contacting people from my home country) since I was busy studying 24/7 and sometimes had days from 6.30am-8pm doing research on research vessels, in the lab etc. The american working culture is a hustle culture and the complete opposite from the danish working culture.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: The american system is very different. Since there are lots of opportunities and offers you might feel overwhelmed and get burned out easily. The experience in the end however is worth it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
